H2962.d: properly, non-occurrence; used adverbially, not yet or before

fb: Man living at the time before the Flood
Cain's line through Lamech and Adah comes down to him and his brother: Jabal is "the father of such as dwell in tents and have cattle", and Jubal is credited with music.

H2983.d: a Jebusite or inhabitant of Jebus

H2974.d: properly, to yield, especially assent; hence (pos.) to undertake as an act of volition

H2909.d: to stretch a bow, as an archer

H2918.d: a wall; hence, a fortress or a hamlet

H2921.d: properly, to cover with pieces; i.e. (by implication) to spot or variegate (as tapestry)

H2966.d: prey, i.e. flocks devoured by animals

H2999.d: Jabbok, a river east of the Jordan
fb: Jacob crossed this stream alone the night before he met Esau, wrestled until daybreak, and came away named Israel and limping. It runs west into the Jordan through a gorge in Gilead, halfway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, and is the Zarqa River today.

H2930.d: to be foul, especially in a ceremial or moral sense (contaminated)

H2945.d: a family (mostly used collectively in the singular)

H2963.d: to pluck off or pull to pieces; causatively to supply with food (as in morsels)

H2975.d: a channel, e.g. a fosse, canal, shaft; specifically the Nile, as the one river of Egypt, including its collateral trenches; also the Tigris, as the main river of Assyria

H2964.d: something torn, i.e. a fragment, e.g. a fresh leaf, prey, food

H2940.d: properly, a taste, i.e. (figuratively) perception; by implication, intelligence; transitively, a mandate

H2912.d: to grind meal; hence, to be a concubine (that being their employment)

H2981.d: produce, i.e. a crop or (figuratively) wealth

H2973.d: properly, to be slack, i.e. (figuratively) to be foolish

H2971.d: Jair, the name of four Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
He judged Israel twenty-two years. His thirty sons rode thirty donkeys and held thirty towns, which says money and reach, not battles won.
Judges names him twice, and he is a judge from the years before the monarchy.
Joshua names him once, and nothing else is recorded.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
A man from the exile and the return, and Esther is the only book that names him.

H2914.d: a boil or ulcer (from the inflammation), especially a tumor in the anus or pudenda (the piles)

H2985.d: Jabin, the name of two Canaanitish kings
fb: King of Hazor, and master of Sisera, whom Deborah and Barak beat. A Psalm still asks God to deal with Israel's enemies as he dealt with Jabin.
Joshua names him once, and he is a king from the years before the monarchy.

H2995.d: Jabneel, the name of two places in Palestine
fb: On Judah's northwestern border near the coast, the town later called Jabneh or Jamnia. Uzziah tore down its walls.
Two towns carry the name, not a man, and this one is on Naphtali's border.

H2928.d: Telem, the name of a place in Idumaea, also of a temple doorkeeper
fb: A town on Judah's southern border, in the list at Joshua 15:24. It may be the Telaim where Saul gathered his army against the Amalekites.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ezra names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.

A town given to Manasseh inside Issachar's borders, where the Canaanites were never driven out. King Ahaziah of Judah took his death wound near there, running from Jehu. It is generally identified with Khirbet Bel'ameh, near Jenin.

H2961.d: properly, dripping; hence, fresh (i.e. recently made such)

H2982.d: Jebus, the original name of Jerusalem
fb: What Jerusalem was called while the Jebusites held it. David took it and made it his capital.
Saul gathered his army here before he went against the Amalekites, in the Negev of Judah. It is probably the Telem of Joshua 15:24.

H2904.d: to pitch over or reel; hence (transitively) to cast down or out

fb: David's son living at the time of United Monarchy
Born to David in Jerusalem, after he was king, and nothing more.

H2972.d: a Jairite or descendant of Jair
fb: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
Ira, who served David as a priest or chief officer, carries this label, which ties him to Jair. He closes the list of David's court officials, after Joab, Benaiah and Jehoshaphat the recorder.
Woman living at the time of United Monarchy
Solomon's daughter, married to Ben-abinadab, one of the twelve officers who fed the court a month each.

H2947.d: a spread of the hand, i.e. a palm-breadth (not 'span' of the fingers); architecturally, a corbel (as a supporting palm)

H2977.d: Joshijah, the name of two Israelites
fb: King living at the time of Divided Monarchy

Made king of Judah at eight after his father Amon was murdered. In his eighteenth year workmen repairing the temple found a forgotten scroll of the law, and its reading set off Judah's last great reform: pagan altars torn down, the priests of the high places killed, and a Passover like none since the judges. He died young at Megiddo, trying to stop the Egyptian army reaching Assyria.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Zechariah names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.

H2970.d: Jaazanjah, the name of four Israelites
fb: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy

More than one man had the name. One is an army captain who came to the new governor after Jerusalem fell, in Kings and again in Jeremiah; another heads the family Jeremiah brought into the temple and offered wine.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
One of 3 men called Jaazaniah. This one is a man from the exile and the return, named once in Ezekiel.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ezekiel names him once, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Levite living at the time of Divided Monarchy
Zerah's son, a Gershonite Levite, in the genealogy of Chronicles. Nothing further is recorded of him.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Jeroham's son, a Benjamite, among the family heads who settled in Jerusalem after the exile.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
After the exile he was one of the Benjamite family heads living in Jerusalem, and that is the extent of him.
Levite living at the time of Exile and Return
He headed a family of temple gatekeepers, and his descendants were still keeping the gates after the exile.

H2900.d: Tobijah, the name of three Israelites and of one Samaritan
fb: Nehemiah's adversary living at the time of Exile and Return
They called him the Ammonite. With Sanballat he mocked Nehemiah's wall and worked against it, and later a priest gave him a room inside the temple courts, so Nehemiah threw him and his things out.
Man living at the time of Exile and Return
Ezra and Nehemiah name him twice, and he is a man from the exile and the return.
Uzziah broke down Jabneh's walls after beating the Philistines. It is the same town as Jabneel, and as Jamnia, or Yavne, it became a centre of Jewish learning after the temple fell in 70 AD.

H2942.d: properly, flavor; figuratively, judgment (both subjective and objective); hence, account (both subjectively and objectively)

H2967.d: a Tarpelite (collectively) or inhabitants of Tarpel, a place in Assyria

H2926.d: properly, to strew over, i.e. (by implication) to cover in or plate (with beams)

H2907.d: to pounce as a bird of prey

H2986.d: properly, to flow; causatively, to bring (especially with pomp)

H2950.d: properly, to stick on as a patch; figuratively, to impute falsely

H2933.d: to be impure in a religious sense

H2910.d: (in the plural only) the kidneys (as being covered); hence (figuratively) the inmost thought

H2954.d: properly, apparently to be thick; figuratively, to be stupid

H2956.d: to drive on; figuratively, to follow close

H2946.d: to flatten out or extend (as a tent); figuratively, to nurse a child (as promotive of growth);

H2911.d: a hand mill; hence, a millstone

H2937.d: to wander; causatively to lead astray

H2953.d: a finger-nail; also a hoof or claw
